+## #796 - Tormach microARC 4: wrapped (simultaneous) A in the PathPilot post
+
+Sources: the four PathPilot Hub readings mkinney recorded on issue #796
+(2026-11-17, PathPilot v2.14.4, 770MX SIM, 4th axis on, "4" 4th Axis"):
+
+1. A is a plain linear axis in degrees, no rollover: from `G0 A350`,
+   `G1 A10 F360` turned back 340 degrees and read 10.000.
+2. G94 on a combined move: `G1 X4 A180 F20` took about 12 s - F is the
+   X Y Z distance only, A follows in the same time.
+3. G93 is accepted and timed: `G93 G1 X4 A180 F5` took about 12 s.
+4. Pure A in G94: `G1 A180 F360` took about 30 s - F is degrees per minute.
+
+Plus the LinuxCNC G-code reference (G93/G94, F). No Fusion/HSMWorks post or
+output was consulted.
+
+- **Decided: the turning XYZA feed is G93 inverse time.** F = 1 / t, t in
+  minutes = max((tip path relative to the part + one rounding step) /
+  programmed feed, |posted dA| / stated A rate), floored to 0.001.
+  **Why:** reading 2 shows G94 times a combined move by X Y Z alone, so a
+  mostly-rotary move would let A run as fast as its tiny XYZ distance
+  allows, and its time would not be the cutting feed relative to the part
+  (the part turns under the tool). G93 lets the post state the time
+  exactly (reading 3). The path bound uses the rounded XYZ/A words the
+  control interpolates, transformed back into the part frame; a turning
+  trajectory can be longer than the straight stream segment. Floored F and
+  the rounding allowance slow a move.
+  **Dropped:** G94 with the #885 `rotaryFeed` "path" cap - it holds the A
+  rate but times the move by the machine XYZ distance, which on a wrapped
+  op is not the tip's speed over the part. `rotaryRate` (the #885 reader of
+  the stated A rate) is reused; its cap function is not.
+- **Decided: an A-only feed stays G94, F in degrees per minute** (reading 4),
+  under the same time law; a feed that does not turn A is today's G94 move.
+  G94 is restated before any motion that is not a G93 feed and at every
+  section end, so cycles, arcs, probes and the next operation never run in
+  G93. G93 rides the G1 line that enters it; each G93 block carries F.
+- **Decided: A is cumulative.** Each target is the stream's angle's
+  equivalent nearest the held one (179 -> 181, 359 -> 361), from reading 1:
+  the control never wraps or takes the short way. The stated travel bounds
+  the count, refused by name past it ("A counts on through 360").
+- **Decided: A is reset between operations, never carried.** Every section
+  already restates its first A as -180..180 after `G53 G0 Z0` (#785); a
+  wrapped op that ended at A300 unwinds there before the next op.
+- **Decided: split a turning move until it stays on its segment.** The
+  machine moves X Y Z in a straight line while A turns linearly, so the tip
+  relative to the part bows off the stream's straight segment. The post
+  splits each turning move into 2^k equal pieces until the bow, sampled at
+  1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of every piece, is within 0.005 mm (0.0002 in); more
+  than 256 pieces is refused by name. Rapids that turn A are split the same
+  way and carry no F.
+- **Decided: the microARC 4 file states `max_normal_speed` 360 deg/min for
+  A.** **Why:** it is the rate the Hub ran as asked (readings 1 and 4); no
+  Tormach page found states a feed rate we could cite with confidence. It is
+  conservative: a faster real table only runs these programs slower than it
+  could. A machine file with no A rate is refused by name ("states no A
+  feed rate"). **Cost to change:** one number in
+  `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`; the goldens regenerate.
+- **Kept: the -360..360 travel.** The Hub runs show no soft limit inside it;
+  PathPilot's real A limits are an open Hub check. A wrap that would count
+  past it is refused, not wrapped back.
+- **Not exercised:** a real 770MX + microARC 4 cut. The PR lists the Hub
+  check to run first.
+
+- **Review fix: bound the posted trajectory, not its endpoint chord.**
+  With posted XYZ interpolated as `m(u)` and posted A as `theta(u)`, the
+  part-relative trajectory is `q(u) = R(theta(u)) m(u)`. Its speed is
+  bounded by the midpoint speed plus one quarter of a uniform bound on
+  `|q''|`: `2 |dtheta| |dm_yz| + dtheta^2 max(|m0_yz|, |m1_yz|)`.
+  Integrating `|u - 1/2|` gives the quarter factor. XYZ rounding and angle
+  rounding are included before evaluating this bound; the existing one-step
+  allowance remains conservative. **Dropped:** the stream chord plus a
+  rounding allowance, which misses the curved path even when its two
+  endpoints coincide. Independent dense interpolation tests pin feed and
+  A rate against the posted words.
+- **Review fix: narrowly compare the wrapped golden across platforms.**
+  Keep line count, word order, modes, XYZ and ordinary feeds exact. Allow
+  at most 0.001 degree in G0/G1 A and 0.04 inverse minutes in turning G93 F,
+  matching the observed last-place A boundary and adjacent-step F swap
+  (116.959 versus 116.921). Comparator pins reject values outside either
+  bound, changed motion words, changed XYZ, missing words and extra lines.
+  The program's independent A-rate and feed checks remain in place.
+  **Dropped:** replacing the golden with Linux output alone, which merely
+  moves the same boundary failure to another platform; broad numeric
+  tolerances, which could hide motion or mode changes.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Write first-continuous-4axis-part.obj: the journal of the guide's demo part.
+
+A closed cylinder along X, 0.680 in across and 1.25 in long, with its free
+end at X 0 and its axis through Y 0, Z 0. It is the finished surface that
+the Rotary Parallel pass of "Your first continuous 4-axis part" cuts on a
+3/4 in bar. Numbers are millimetres (an OBJ file has no unit).
+
+Provenance: CamCraft's own demo geometry; no vendor material.
+Run: python3 examples/models/gen_first_continuous_4axis_part_obj.py
+"""
+
+from math import cos, pi, sin
+from pathlib import Path
+
+IN = 25.4
+RADIUS = 0.340 * IN
+LENGTH = 1.25 * IN
+SIDES = 96
+
+
+def solid(name, title, rings):
+    """A closed solid of revolution about X through the (x, radius) rings."""
+    lines = [
+        f"# CamCraft example: {title} (millimetres)",
+        "# Made by gen_first_continuous_4axis_part_obj.py - do not edit by hand",
+        f"o {name}",
+    ]
+    for x, r in rings:
+        for j in range(SIDES):
+            t = 2.0 * pi * j / SIDES
+            lines.append(f"v {x:.6f} {r * cos(t):.6f} {r * sin(t):.6f}")
+    lines.append(f"v {rings[0][0]:.6f} 0.000000 0.000000")
+    lines.append(f"v {rings[-1][0]:.6f} 0.000000 0.000000")
+    back, front = len(rings) * SIDES + 1, len(rings) * SIDES + 2
+    last = (len(rings) - 1) * SIDES
+    for j in range(SIDES):
+        k = (j + 1) % SIDES
+        for ring in range(len(rings) - 1):
+            a0, a1 = ring * SIDES + j + 1, ring * SIDES + k + 1
+            b0, b1 = a0 + SIDES, a1 + SIDES
+            lines.append(f"f {a0} {a1} {b1}")
+            lines.append(f"f {a0} {b1} {b0}")
+        lines.append(f"f {back} {k + 1} {j + 1}")
+        lines.append(f"f {front} {last + j + 1} {last + k + 1}")
+    Path(__file__).with_name(name + ".obj").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+
+
+def main():
+    # From the chuck side to the free end.
+    solid("first-continuous-4axis-part", "Your first continuous 4-axis part",
+          [(-LENGTH, RADIUS), (0.0, RADIUS)])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

++++
+title = "Your first continuous 4-axis program"
+description = "Set up, post and air-cut a Rotary Parallel program on the Tormach 770MX and the microARC 4, with the A axis turning during the feed moves."
+weight = 7
++++
+
+This guide takes one small job from start to finish on a **Tormach 770MX**
+with a **microARC 4** rotary table: a Rotary Parallel pass along a round
+bar. The work is *continuous* 4-axis: the A axis turns inside the
+operation, and on some feed moves it turns together with X, Y and Z. For
+*indexed* work, where A stops before each cut, see
+[Your first 4-axis part](@/guide/getting-started/first-4axis-part.md).
+
+**This program is for an air cut only. Do not cut a bar with it.** Rotary
+Parallel finishes the two end faces of the model down to the A centreline.
+At the chuck end, the bar goes on into the jaws, so that pass is a cut
+through the bar (issue
+[#2343](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2343)). The guide thus
+ends with a run in the PathPilot simulator and an air cut with no bar in
+the chuck. Those two runs prove what a continuous program must prove first:
+that the control reads the A words, the `G93` feeds and the `G94` return as
+the post wrote them.
+
+The continuous output of `tormach.cps` is new (issue
+[#796](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/796)). It was written
+from four test moves in the PathPilot simulator. No complete program has
+been run in the simulator or on a machine yet.
+
+You need the machine file `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` and the post
+`tormach.cps`. Both ship with CamCraft, as the machine
+`Tormach 770MX + microARC 4` and the post `Tormach PathPilot`.
+
+Companion files in the repository:
+
+- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`: the finished project.
+- `examples/models/first-continuous-4axis-part.obj`: the model.
+- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`: the program that the project
+  posts. Each G-code excerpt on this page is copied from this file.
+
+Open the project in the app with **Open**, or post it from the
+[command line](@/guide/automate/cli.md):
+
+```text
+camcraft-cli process examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj -o first-continuous-4axis-part.nc
+```
+
+## The job and how the bar is held
+
+The stock is a 3/4 in round bar in the microARC 4 chuck, with 2 in out of
+the jaws. The model is a plain cylinder, 0.680 in across and 1.25 in long,
+at the free end of the bar. One operation, a Rotary Parallel pass with a
+1/8 in ball tool, finishes the model.
+
+![Side and end views of the bar in the chuck: G54 X0 at the free end face, Y0 and Z0 on the A centreline, and the model as a dashed outline.](../../../guide-pictures/first-continuous-4axis-setup.svg)
+
+The bar axis is the X axis, because the microARC 4 turns about X. The work
+offset G54 is at the free end of the bar, on the A centreline.
+
+## Machine, post and unit
+
+1. **Mount the machine.** In the browser, click the **Machine** row. In the
+   **Library** list, pick `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4`.
+2. **Pick the post.** In the browser, click the **Post** row and pick
+   `Tormach PathPilot` in the list.
+3. **Set the unit.** Click {{ <icon name="tree-stock" /> }} **Stock** in the ribbon. In the **Units** row,
+   choose **Inches**. This program starts with `G20`.
+
+The machine file states four things about the A axis. Compare each one with
+your machine before you trust a program:
+
+| In the machine file | Value | What uses it |
+|---|---|---|
+| A rotary about X | `axis` 1, 0, 0 | The operation's fitted axis must be on this line. The posted letter is A. |
+| A travel | -360 to 360 degrees | The machine check and the post. A count past it is refused. |
+| `nose_to_axis` | 10.6 (inches) | The [index swing check](@/guide/multi-axis/checks.md). It is the catalogue distance from the spindle nose to the A centreline at the top of Z. |
+| A `max_normal_speed` | 360 (degrees per minute) | The post holds each turn of A to this rate. A machine file with no A rate is refused. |
+
+The A rate of 360 degrees per minute is the rate that the PathPilot
+simulator ran in the test moves. It is not a figure from Tormach. The A
+travel is not checked against PathPilot's own limits. If your machine has
+other values, edit a copy of the machine file: see
+[Machine types](@/guide/check-and-post/machines.md).
+
+## Model, stock and work offset
+
+1. **Import the model.** Click {{ <icon name="folder-open" /> }} **Model** and pick
+   `examples/models/first-continuous-4axis-part.obj`. An OBJ file has no
+   unit and CamCraft reads its numbers as millimetres. The model's axis is
+   the X axis. Its free end is at X 0 and the axis goes through Y 0, Z 0.
+2. **Set the stock.** On the Stock page, choose **Box**. Type
+   **Length (X)** 2, **Width (Y)** 0.75 and **Height (Z)** 0.75, then
+   **X center** -1, **Y center** 0 and **Z bottom** -0.375. Click
+   **Apply**. The box is the 2 in of bar that is out of the jaws. A
+   Cylinder stock always stands along Z, so it cannot be a bar along X.
+3. **Check the work offset.** Click {{ <icon name="tree-wcs" /> }} **Origin**. Keep **X origin**,
+   **Y origin** and **Z origin** at 0.
+
+You do not tell CamCraft where the rotary is. A rotary operation fits the
+axis of revolution from the model, and that axis must be on the line of the
+machine's A axis. The post then turns each point about the work offset. Thus
+G54 Y0 and Z0 must be on the line that the table turns about. On the
+machine:
+
+- Set G54 X0 at the free end face of the bar.
+- Find the A centreline in Y: indicate the two sides of a round bar in the
+  chuck and take the middle. Set G54 Y0 there.
+- Find the A centreline in Z: touch the top of the bar and subtract its
+  radius, 0.375 in. Set G54 Z0 there. Z0 is the centre of the bar, not its
+  top.
+- Check it: turn A by 180 degrees and indicate the bar again. If the two
+  readings are different, the bar does not run true in the chuck, and half
+  of the difference is the error of your centreline.
+- Set A to 0 where you want it. This job has no feature that needs one
+  angle, but the program's first A move is absolute.
+
+## The tool
+
+Click {{ <icon name="tools" /> }} **Tools**, then **New tool…**. Set **Type** to **Ball nose** and
+type these values:
+
+| Field | T1 |
+|---|---|
+| **Name** | BN 1/8 |
+| **Diameter** | 0.125 |
+| **Flute length** | 0.625 |
+| **Shank diameter** | 0.125 |
+| **Spindle rpm** | 8000 |
+| Feed (in/min) | 8 |
+
+Choose **Add tool**. The speed and the feeds in this project are the
+example's numbers. They are not a recommendation for your machine, tool or
+material.
+
+The flute is long because of the end faces. See
+[Check it](#check-it).
+
+## The operation
+
+Add a {{ <icon name="op-rotary-parallel" /> }} **Rotary Parallel** from the **Multi-axis** group. Set its
+**Tool** to BN 1/8 and its **Source** to the model,
+`first-continuous-4axis-part`. Click **Rename**, type `Journal` and choose
+**Apply name**. Then set these values:
+
+| Tab | Setting | Value |
+|---|---|---|
+| **Heights** | **Clearance Z** | **From** Fixed value, **Offset** 0.875 |

+| **Heights** | **Bottom Z** | **From** Fixed value, **Offset** -0.375 |

+## What the post refuses
+
+`tormach.cps` refuses these cases by name and writes no file:
+
+| Case | The refusal contains |
+|---|---|
+| A changes inside one operation, but the machine file states no A rate | `simultaneous 4-axis motion` ... `states no A feed rate` |
+| A turns one way past the A travel | `A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over)` |
+| An arc, a canned cycle or a probe move that would turn A | `the post writes a turning A on straight G0 / G1 moves only` |
+| A move that turns A from a start point the post does not know | `its path and time cannot be judged` |
+| A move that turns A and cannot be split fine enough to stay on its path | `still bows` |
+| A tilt that an A about X cannot make (a B or C lean) | `the A axis about X cannot reach it` |

+The last but one row is about the path between two points. The machine
+moves X, Y and Z in a straight line while A turns, so the tool does not go
+straight across the part. The post splits each such move into shorter
+moves until the error is less than 0.0002 in. This is why the program has
+many short `G93` lines.
+
+A refusal is not an error in your project. It says that the post cannot
+write a safe program for the case. See
+[Reading a refusal](@/guide/reference/refusals.md).

+def a_count_picture():
+    data = [(number, end[2], g93) for number, _, _, end, g93 in moves() if end[2] is not None]
+    last = sum(1 for _ in PROGRAM.read_text().splitlines())
+    left, right, top, bottom = 70.0, 690.0, 40.0, 250.0
+    px = lambda line: n(left + (right - left) * line / last)
+    py = lambda a: n(bottom - (bottom - top) * (a + 360.0) / 720.0)
+    body = ['<text x="20" y="24">The A word, line by line (degrees)</text>']
+    for a in (-360, -180, 0, 180, 360):
+        cls = "limit" if abs(a) == 360 else "grid"
+        body.append(f'<path class="{cls}" d="M{n(left)} {py(a)} H{n(right)}"/>')
+        body.append(f'<text class="small" x="{n(left - 8)}" y="{n(float(py(a)) + 4)}" text-anchor="end">{a}</text>')
+    body.append(f'<text class="small" x="{n(right)}" y="{n(float(py(360)) - 6)}" text-anchor="end">A travel in the machine file: -360 to 360</text>')
+    points = " ".join(f"{px(line)},{py(a)}" for line, a, _ in data)
+    body.append(f'<polyline class="cut" points="{points}"/>')
+    hi = max(data, key=lambda d: d[1])
+    lo = min(data, key=lambda d: d[1])
+    body.append(f'<text class="small" x="{px(hi[0])}" y="{n(float(py(hi[1])) - 8)}" text-anchor="middle">A{hi[1]:g}</text>')

+    body.append(f'<path d="{ticks}" stroke="#006ba6" stroke-width="1" fill="none"/>')
+    body.append(f'<text class="small" x="{n(left - 8)}" y="271" text-anchor="end">G93</text>')

+def paths_picture():
+    (_, _), (length, _) = stock_and_journal()
+    left, right, top, bottom = 70.0, 690.0, 40.0, 300.0
+    x_lo, x_hi, a_lo, a_hi = -1.4, 0.15, -90.0, 270.0
+    px = lambda x: n(left + (right - left) * (x - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo))
+    py = lambda a: n(bottom - (bottom - top) * (a - a_lo) / (a_hi - a_lo))
+    body = ['<text x="20" y="24">Each move, unrolled: X along the bar against the A angle</text>']
+    for a in (-90, 0, 90, 180, 270):
+        body.append(f'<path class="grid" d="M{n(left)} {py(a)} H{n(right)}"/>')
+        body.append(f'<text class="small" x="{n(left - 8)}" y="{n(float(py(a)) + 4)}" text-anchor="end">A{a}</text>')
+    for x, label in ((-length, f"X-{length:g}: chuck-side end"), (0.0, "X0: free end")):
+        body.append(f'<path class="limit" d="M{px(x)} {n(top)} V{n(bottom)}"/>')
+        anchor = "start" if x < 0 else "end"
+        body.append(f'<text class="small" x="{px(x)}" y="{n(bottom + 18)}" text-anchor="{anchor}">{label}</text>')

+    body.append(f'<path class="cut" style="stroke-width:1.2" d="{"".join(feed)}"/>')
+    body.append(f'<path class="cut" d="M{n(left)} 330 h30"/><text class="small" x="{n(left + 38)}" y="334">feed (G1)</text>')
+    body.append(f'<path class="link" d="M{n(left + 130)} 330 h30"/><text class="small" x="{n(left + 168)}" y="334">rapid (G0)</text>')
